newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close lower on new baht measures.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close lower on new baht measures.

text.p: Thai stocks closed lower in thin trade on Wednesday as foreign investors were sidelined by cental bank moves to prevent speculators from repatriating baht funds obtained from the bourse, brokers said.
"Foreigners were not active today. They were not happy with the central bank measures which, they believed, would leave them with smaller profits," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The composite SET index declined 5.82 points to a 97-month low of 521.40 on tiny 2.3 billion baht turnover.

New measures announced by the Bank of Thailand on Tuesday required bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks from foreigners and non-resident investors selling Thai stocks must remit funds in foreign currencies only.
The measures were imposed to cut off supply sources for baht speculators following the last attack on the baht in mid-May.
The SET-50 index declined 0.50 point to 37.02
Most of the key sectors retreated on Wednesday. The banking counter was first-ranked in terms of value, falling 2.95 percent, followed by the communication sector, which fell 0.80 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, falling five baht to 144.

TPI Polene, which announced it would delay construction of its fourth cement plant and a power plant because of the sluggish Thai economy, shed 0.25 baht to 18, Shinawatra Computer gained five to 110 and PTT Exploration rose two to 328.
